record.original_question: For every generalized minimal flow whose vorticity domain decomposes numerically into blobs B_1,...,B_N and a background region B_0, is curl u constant on the background B_0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a two-dimensional flow domain (for instance the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^2$) and let $u$ be a smooth divergence-free vector field on $M$ with scalar vorticity $\omega = \operatorname{curl} u$. Call $u$ a generalized minimal flow (GM-flow) if it is a critical point of the $L^2$-norm of vorticity restricted to the coadjoint orbit of $\omega$ under the action of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms; equivalently, every field $\tilde u$ whose vorticity is obtained from $\omega$ by an area-preserving rearrangement satisfies $\|\operatorname{curl}\tilde u\|_{L^2} \ge \|\operatorname{curl} u\|_{L^2}$ at the infinitesimal level. Suppose the vorticity configuration of such a GM-flow decomposes into finitely many "vorticity blobs" $B_1,\dots,B_N \subset M$ (compactly supported regions on which $\omega$ takes non-trivial, localized profiles) together with a complementary "background" region $B_0 = M \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^N B_i$.

Question: Must $\operatorname{curl} u$ be constant on the background region $B_0$ for every such GM-flow?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as a stated open conjecture in the survey of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics, with numerical evidence motivating it. No subsequent resolution was found in the search results.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems (arXiv:2205.01143)
status_evidence.snippet: The flow domain contains vorticity blobs B_1,...,B_N and a background B_0, with the conjecture that for any GM-flow the curl of velocity equals a constant in B_0.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open conjecture in the geometric hydrodynamics open-problems survey.
